whyCorrect: Read the goal literally: it asks you to emphasize the difference between the two works, so the right choice has to set one work against the other on some point where the notes actually disagree. The notes give you exactly that contrast — the Women's Table is a memorial sculpture, and Untitled is an installation artwork. Choice C puts those two facts on either side of "while," a contrast word, so the sentence's whole structure is the difference. Nothing else in the choice competes with that job, which is why it beats options that pile on more detail.

whyWrong.A: This groups the two works together as examples of the same career — "such as" lists them as alike rather than contrasting them, so it satisfies a goal about what Lin is known for, not about how the works differ.
whyWrong.B: This emphasizes a similarity, not a difference: it says both are large-scale works. It also misreports the notes, since only Untitled was completed in 1997 and "respectively" is left with a single date to distribute.
whyWrong.D: The concession "Though Untitled is not a memorial" is only setup; the main clause says the one work may call the other to mind, so the sentence lands on resemblance in scale rather than on difference. It also alters the notes' thirty-two-ton figure to thirty-ton.

commonMistakes: Choosing the longest, most detailed choice — D uses the most information from the notes, but a synthesis question is scored on whether the sentence does the stated job, not on how much of the notes it packs in.
tips: Before reading the choices, name the goal in your own words as a test, here "does this sentence contrast the two works?", then check each choice against that one test.
